title: Isomorphisms in the category of weird inverse systems are detected by bounded torsion kernels and cokernels
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes isomorphisms in the category of the weird systems remark: a morphism (c, phi_n) is an isomorphism if and only if there is c' >= 0 such that the kernel and cokernel of phi_n are I^{c'}-torsion for all sufficiently large n (source lines 29167-29174). The proof is an explicit construction of an inverse. It first assumes, without loss of generality, that c' >= c and that the kernel and cokernel of every phi_n are I^{c'}-torsion (proof lines 29177-29179). For n >= c' and x in I^{c'}E'_n it chooses y in I^cE_n with x congruent to phi_n(y) modulo E'_n[I^c], possible because the cokernel is annihilated by I^{c'}, and sets psi_n(x) to be the class of y in E_n/E_n[I^{c'}] (proof lines 29180-29183). The substantive step is well-definedness: for another choice y' with the same congruence the difference y - y' maps to zero in E'_n/E'_n[I^c] and hence is annihilated by I^{c'} in I^cE_n, so psi_n is independent of the choice (proof lines 29183-29188). The author then omits the verification that (c', psi_n) is the inverse of (c, phi_n) in the category (proof lines 29189-29190). The non-routine content is the lifting step and the well-definedness argument, both of which depend on reading the torsion conditions at the correct exponents; note that the author leaves the final composition check to the reader.
